content: Zanamivir is a medication prescribed specifically for your current condition and should not be used for other purposes unless directed by your healthcare provider. It is not a replacement for the flu vaccine. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is within two hours of your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Store this medication at room temperature in a dry place. Do not puncture the foil blister until you are ready to use it. Avoid storing it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. Zanamivir is used to treat symptoms caused by the influenza virus (flu) if symptoms have been present for two days or less. It may also be used to prevent the flu if you have been exposed to someone with the flu, such as a sick household member, or during a community flu outbreak. This medication works by inhibiting the growth of the flu virus. Before using zanamivir, read the patient information leaflet provided by your pharmacist. Follow all usage instructions carefully. For flu treatment, inhale this medication through your mouth as directed by your doctor, typically two inhalations (one blister per inhalation) twice daily, approximately 12 hours apart, for five days. For flu prevention, inhale two inhalations (one blister per inhalation) once daily as directed by your doctor. To use the disk inhaler, remove the cover and check the mouthpiece to ensure it is clean and free of particles. Load the medication disk into the inhaler and puncture one medication blister. Keep the inhaler level to prevent spilling the medication. Exhale fully through your mouth, place the mouthpiece into your mouth, and inhale deeply to draw the medication into your lungs. Hold your breath for a few seconds. If another inhalation is required, advance to the next blister and repeat the process. Start using zanamivir as soon as possible for optimal effectiveness. It works best when the medication level in your body is maintained consistently. Continue using it for the full prescribed duration, even if your symptoms improve. If you have breathing problems such as asthma or chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and are scheduled to use inhaled bronchodilators (e.g., albuterol) at the same time as zanamivir, use the bronchodilator first before using zanamivir. Dizziness may occur as a side effect of this medication. Additionally, because it is an inhaled powder, you may experience increased coughing after use. This medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks. However, zanamivir can cause breathing problems, which in rare cases may be severe or even fatal. If you experience wheezing or shortness of breath, stop using zanamivir and seek medical attention immediately. Zanamivir is not recommended for individuals with lung or breathing problems. Discuss the risks and benefits with your doctor. Rarely, the flu itself or zanamivir may cause serious mental or mood changes, which may be more likely in children. Severe allergic reactions to this drug are rare. If you experience symptoms such as rash, itching, swelling (especially of the face, tongue, or throat), severe dizziness, or trouble breathing, seek medical help immediately. This is not a complete list of possible side effects. In the U.S., contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for medical advice about side effects. Before using zanamivir, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients (such as lactose or milk proteins) that can cause allergic reactions or other problems. This drug may cause dizziness, and alcohol or marijuana (cannabis) can exacerbate this effect. Avoid driving, using machinery, or performing tasks requiring alertness until you can do so safely. Limit alcoholic beverages. This medication may be less effective in young children. During pregnancy, zanamivir should only be used when clearly needed. It is unknown if this drug passes into breast milk. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase your risk for serious side effects. Keep a list of all the products you use (including prescription and nonprescription drugs and herbal products) and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Inform your doctor if you have received a nasal flu vaccine in the past two weeks, as zanamivir may interfere with the vaccine's effectiveness if administered too closely together. In case of overdose, if someone has serious symptoms such as passing out or trouble breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs.
